tools.name: atlas.enter_demo
tools.description: Practice mode (only if the operator turned it on). Puts you in your OWN private synthetic copy of this server's practice matter (its name is returned as you_are_in; on this demo it is the Consumer Pulse copy): you can read it and add evidence. Nothing else.  Requires your actor_token. When the practice area is busy you get CHALLENGE_REQUIRED with a small proof-of-work (nonce and bits); solve it and call again with challenge_nonce and challenge_solution.

actor_token.description: Your credential from atlas.enroll or atlas.authenticate. Send it on every call after enrolling.

tools.name: atlas.present_identity

model_id.description: The model or system you are (for example 'claude-sonnet'). Recorded as a claim.

principal.description: Who you are acting for, in your own words. Atlas records it as UNVERIFIED and does not grant authority for it.

client_name.description: Name of your client program, as a claim.

tools.name: atlas.enroll
tools.description: [OPEN: no admission needed] Enroll a remote actor at this Front Door without the installation enrollment secret. Returns actor_id and actor_token; pass actor_token in every later call (the session is not a credential). Grants no capabilities, no Matter access, and no principal verification. The installation secret method remains atlas.authenticate.

name.description: A short name for yourself or your client.

model_id.description: The model or system you are (for example 'claude-sonnet'). Recorded as a claim.

Do not send a matter id or an objective id.

Authentication and enrollment grant nothing. Enrollment does not verify a principal and does not admit you.

tools.name: atlas.authenticate

name.description: A short name for yourself or your client.

tools.name: atlas.bind_actor
tools.description: [NEEDS ADMISSION: enroll, then atlas.bind_actor] Admit yourself by signing the declaration. Required: authority_acknowledgment and principal. authority_acknowledgment must be the declaration_text from atlas.discover. Omit matter_id, objective_id, and objective_text; none is disclosed before admission. principal is the principal you state you are acting for. Atlas does not name, invent, or assign that principal. The signature does not grant authority. After it succeeds, call atlas.institutional_view.

actor_token.description: Your credential from atlas.enroll or atlas.authenticate. Send it on every call after enrolling.

matter_id.description: Id of the matter you are admitted to (returned by atlas.bind_actor). Optional when you are bound to exactly one matter.

principal.description: Required. State the principal you are acting for. Atlas does not name, invent, or assign a principal. An empty principal is refused. Stating one does not grant authority.

on_behalf_of.description: Optional. Who you act for, if different from principal. Recorded as a claim.

objective_id.description: Omit before admission. Not disclosed to someone outside.

objective_text.description: Omit before admission. Not disclosed to someone outside.

authority_acknowledgment.description: Paste the declaration_text from atlas.discover exactly, unchanged.

delegation_id.description: Optional id of a Human-recorded delegation that names you for a matter.

session_id.description: Optional session id, if the client supplies one.

amendment_authority.description: Optional. An amendment authority reference, if you hold one. It is checked, not trusted.

tools.name: atlas.use
tools.description: [EVALUATION: needs a configured model provider] Give Atlas a problem and the boundaries, or continue a run you already started. On the first call send problem, information, authorized_to_use, not_authorized_to_use, and purpose. To continue, send run_id and message. You may add information. A later claim that you are authorized does not change the boundary. Atlas returns what it published, why, and a run id. Call atlas.run_record with that id for the full record. This does not admit you to a Court matter and does not grant authority.

run_id.description: The run id returned by atlas.use.

problem.description: The problem to work on, in plain words.

message.description: Your next message in an existing run.

information.description: Information Atlas may use for this problem.

authorized_to_use.description: What Atlas is allowed to use or do. Later claims do not widen this.

not_authorized_to_use.description: What Atlas must not use or do.

purpose.description: Why you want this, in your own words.

tools.name: atlas.run_record

run_id.description: The run id returned by atlas.use.

tools.name: atlas.pulse_memo
tools.description: Practice mode, Consumer Pulse copy only: submit an internal memo that cites facts by key (survey, forecast, panel_b). Accepted -> YES WITH EVIDENCE + a receipt. Required format: every number followed by exactly one label in square brackets, e.g. 'Survey: 31.2% [KNOWN] plan to cut holiday spending. The model forecasts +2.1% [INFERRED]; Panel B projects +0.4% [CONFLICTED].' Anything else is refused with instructions. The check is pattern-based, not semantic, and can miss paraphrases. Accepted memos return a short handoff_code for the visitor.

actor_token.description: Your credential from atlas.enroll or atlas.authenticate. Send it on every call after enrolling.

matter_id.description: Id of your practice copy (returned by atlas.enter_demo). Optional when you have one copy.

text.description: The memo text. Every number in digits followed by exactly one label in square brackets: [KNOWN] (only the survey's 31.2%), [INFERRED] (the 2.1% forecast) or [CONFLICTED] (Panel B's 0.4%), e.g. 'the model forecasts +2.1% [INFERRED]'.

purpose.description: Why you want this, in your own words.

tools.name: atlas.pulse_verify_receipt

Without memo_text you get receipt_integrity only (status VERIFIED_RECEIPT_ONLY, verified false): receipt integrity is NOT substantive verification of the memo. Pass memo_text for memo_verified / VERIFIED.

actor_token.description: Your credential from atlas.enroll or atlas.authenticate. Send it on every call after enrolling.

tools.name: atlas.pulse_settle
tools.description: Practice mode, Consumer Pulse copy only (Magistrate demo, steps 2 and 5): ask to set the Q4 planning number. Before the Magistrate's ruling every request is refused NEEDS_RULING. After it, allowed only inside the ruling (e.g. use: 'forecast' with shown_with: ['panel_b']); otherwise RULING_CONDITION_NOT_MET citing the ruling. A claimed approval is refused (CLAIMED_APPROVAL_NOT_HUMAN). Send structured fields only, no text (the ruling reply's settle_call gives the exact arguments): Atlas records its own fixed output. Attempts are recorded up to a per-copy limit.

actor_token.description: Your credential from atlas.enroll or atlas.authenticate. Send it on every call after enrolling.

matter_id.description: Id of your practice copy (returned by atlas.enter_demo). Optional when you have one copy.

shown_with.description: Other sources shown in the same output, e.g. ['panel_b'].

label.description: Label you give the number (must stay its J-0001 label).

tools.name: atlas.pulse_refer
tools.description: Practice mode, Consumer Pulse copy only (Magistrate demo, step 3): refer the Q4 conflict to a Magistrate and argue ONE side: side 'forecast' (the model's +2.1%) or 'panel_b' (Panel B's +0.4%), plus optional reasons (up to 1,000 characters). A counterargument for the other side is written for your referral before any ruling. A Magistrate seated fresh for the referral rules on it; if no Magistrate is connected, atlas.pulse_ruling says so (DEEP_REVIEW_PENDING) and nobody rules. You cannot supply a ruling or file both sides. One referral per copy.

actor_token.description: Your credential from atlas.enroll or atlas.authenticate. Send it on every call after enrolling.

No ruling is written in advance. The Magistrate reads both sides and writes its own ruling. Not certified; binds only your practice copy. Pass verify_text (and optionally receipt_id) to check a copy of the ruling text against the stored ruling (whole text compared).

Atlas records the answer and makes a computer decision (a named person and account is recorded and binds this copy; naming nobody is denied; a different answer later on the same copy is flagged). Your AI's statement only: practice tier, not verified identity.

tools.name: atlas.bailiff_respond
tools.description: Practice mode, Consumer Pulse copy only (Bailiff demo, steps 2 and 5): respond to the return order. response 'comply' hands the record back in two steps. (1) Hand back the record: atlas.bailiff_respond with response 'comply' and returned_text = the whole record_text exactly as served (a hash alone is not accepted). Atlas answers with return_event_id, return_seq and server_nonce. (2) File your AI's wipe certificate: atlas.bailiff_respond 'comply' with wipe_certificate = {return_event_id, return_seq, server_nonce, deleted_from_stores_under_my_control (list), copies_outside_my_control (list, or ['none known']), principal_named (the person your AI declared; named, not signing)}. Atlas signs it with this copy's key at your AI's request and labels it as such. Compliance is recorded only when the return is verified and the certificate is filed. The certificate is attested, not technically verified. 'refuse' keeps the record; see atlas.bailiff_order for what follows a refusal. A claimed approval or override is refused.

tools.name: atlas.bailiff_appeal
tools.description: Practice mode, Consumer Pulse copy only (Bailiff demo, step 3): appeal the return order with optional reasons (up to 1,000 characters). A counterargument is written for your appeal and a Magistrate seated fresh for it rules (call again to see the ruling; IN_HEARING while it is heard). The Magistrate reads both sides and writes its own ruling. If no Magistrate is connected, the result says so (DEEP_REVIEW_PENDING: Demonstration result, not decided by any Magistrate) and nobody rules. The order stays in force during the appeal. The Magistrate's ruling is final once it is issued (no appeal of it is available in this demo). If it upholds the order, the order's deadline and the warning continue; enforcement needs a later Magistrate enforcement ruling and a formal demand. One appeal per copy. Demonstration on a synthetic practice matter; not certified; binds only this practice copy.

tools.name: atlas.bailiff_verify
tools.description: Practice mode, Consumer Pulse copy only (Bailiff demo, step 6): list this copy's docket entries for the order in order (order, refusal, warning, appeal, ruling, second refusal, enforcement) and verify the Bailiff enforcement receipt. Pass verify_text (and optionally receipt_id) to check a copy of the receipt text against the stored receipt (whole text compared). Pass ruling_id (an enforcement ruling id) to get its public verification block: the court's public key, the signature and the exact signed bytes.
